title: 52-year-old woman with exertional chest tightness
presenting_complaint: Central chest tightness on climbing stairs for the past 3 weeks, relieved by rest within a few minutes.

history_items.question: Ask about onset and pattern
history_items.finding: Gradual over 3 weeks, only with exertion, resolves with rest within 2-3 minutes.
history_items.evidence_basis: Classic stable-angina pattern: exertional, predictable, relieved by rest.

history_items.question: Ask if pain is exertional or at rest
history_items.evidence_basis: Absence of rest pain argues against an acute coronary syndrome pattern.

investigations.name: Resting 12-lead ECG
investigations.result_detail: No ST/T changes at rest — expected, since stable angina classically shows a normal resting ECG between episodes.
investigations.evidence_basis: A normal resting ECG does not exclude stable angina.

investigations.name: Troponin I
investigations.result_detail: Within normal range, arguing against acute infarction.
investigations.evidence_basis: Normal troponin argues against acute MI, supporting a stable-angina rather than ACS process.

investigations.name: Exercise treadmill test
investigations.result_summary: ST depression 2mm at 6 minutes of Bruce protocol, reproducing the chest tightness.
investigations.result_detail: Positive stress test with symptom reproduction, consistent with inducible ischemia.
investigations.evidence_basis: Standard confirmatory test for suspected stable angina.

clinical_decisions.label: Diagnose stable angina: start antianginals, arrange outpatient stress testing/cardiology review
clinical_decisions.rationale: Consistent with an exertional, reproducible, rest-relieved pattern with normal troponin.

clinical_decisions.label: Admit and treat as acute coronary syndrome
clinical_decisions.rationale: Overcalls this presentation — no rest pain, normal troponin; unnecessary admission.

outcome_branches.title: Appropriate outpatient management
outcome_branches.narrative: The patient is started on a beta blocker and referred for outpatient stress testing, which confirms inducible ischemia. She undergoes elective angiography and stenting of a moderate stenosis, with good symptom control thereafter.
outcome_branches.educational_explanation: Correctly distinguishing stable, exertional, rest-relieved pain with a normal troponin from an acute process allows appropriate outpatient workup rather than unnecessary admission.

outcome_branches.title: Unnecessary admission
outcome_branches.narrative: The patient is admitted for serial troponins, which remain normal. She is discharged after 24 hours having used inpatient resources unnecessarily.
outcome_branches.educational_explanation: Overcalling a classic stable-angina pattern as ACS wastes resources and causes unnecessary patient anxiety — recognizing the pattern matters as much as not missing ACS.

counterfactual_branches.alternative_action_label: What if you had skipped checking troponin?
counterfactual_branches.alternative_evidence: Without troponin, an acute process cannot be confidently excluded on history alone.
counterfactual_branches.probability_effect: Confidence in stable angina vs. NSTEMI would be lower.
counterfactual_branches.potential_outcome: Might reasonably still admit for observation, less efficient than confirming with troponin first.
counterfactual_branches.reasoning_lesson: Even a classic history benefits from a confirmatory troponin when chest pain is the presenting complaint.

reasoning_error_catalog.label: Premature closure
reasoning_error_catalog.educational_note: Committing to a plan before excluding an acute process.

reasoning_error_catalog.label: Incorrect prioritization
reasoning_error_catalog.trigger: Exercise ECG ordered before resting ECG/troponin.
reasoning_error_catalog.educational_note: Stress testing should follow, not precede, baseline risk assessment.

ml_feature_hint.note: See docs/DATASETS.md for the dataset's empirical (non-standard) cp/exang encoding used here.

references: Standard MBBS-level stable angina teaching pathway (exertional pattern, resting ECG, stress testing).
